The langeleik is a Norwegian folk chordophone of the zither family, Hornbostel–Sachs number 314.122-6. The body has one melody string and up to eight drone strings; under the melody string there are seven frets to the octave, giving the natural major scale, and the drone strings are tuned to a triad. The player strikes the rhythm with a long pick in the right hand and stops or plucks the strings with the index, middle and ring fingers of the left. It is mostly used for Norwegian country dances and solo playing, such as the waltz, mazurka and springar.

The German scheitholt and the Swedish hummel were once regarded as its forerunners, but in 1980 an instrument dating from 1524 was found at the Vibergsroa farm in Gjøvik in Norway, earlier than the documentary record of those instruments. Older types used Pythagorean tuning, based on pure fifths and octaves, so intervals could vary and the melody could move between darker low intervals and a bright major. After 1850 a fixed major type appeared, and old repertoire therefore had to be rewritten or new tunes sought. The modern body is wider at the middle and louder, and is tuned uniformly to the major; Valdres and Vardal keep a livelier tradition, while Telemark has a thin, straight-walled body and a different pegbox.
朗格萊克琴為挪威持續音齊特琴，Hornbostel–Sachs編號314.122: The langeleik is a Norwegian drone zither, Hornbostel–Sachs number 314.122-6. It sounds from one melody string with up to eight drone strings, the drones tuned to a triad and sounding together with the melody to make a thicker sound. Seven frets to the octave give the natural major scale, so it cannot play chromatically or change key easily, and pitch and harmonic change are limited. Early types could use special scales, with a third that was more or less neutral and a low seventh; modern types are mostly tuned to the major scale, with the middle of the body wider to increase volume. The Telemark type has a thin, straight-walled box without a bottom and relies more on the soundboard, while the Valdres type is wider at the lower end. The right hand strikes the basic beat with a long pick.
